Burroughs Large Systems.fact: The change in external datacommunications hardware did not require any change to existing MCS (Message Control System (discussed below)) software.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: On input, messages were passed from the DCP via an internal bus to the relevant MCP _____ (DCC) DCP process stack
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: On input, messages were passed from the DCP via an internal bus to the relevant MCP Datacom Control (DCC) DCP process stack.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: An MCS may be considered to be a middleware program and is written in DCALGOL (_____ ALGOL)
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: An MCS may be considered to be a middleware program and is written in DCALGOL (Data Communications ALGOL).

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: As stated above, the MCS received messages from queues maintained by the _____ (DCC) and forwarded these messages to the appropriate application/function for processing
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: As stated above, the MCS received messages from queues maintained by the Datacom Control Stack (DCC) and forwarded these messages to the appropriate application/function for processing.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: One of the original MCS's was CANDE (_____ AND Edit) which was developed as the online program development environment
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: One of the original MCS's was CANDE (Command AND Edit) which was developed as the online program development environment.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: Another MCS named COMS was introduced around _____ and developed as a high performance transaction processing control system
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: Another MCS named COMS was introduced around 1984 and developed as a high performance transaction processing control system.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: There were predecessor transaction processing environments which included GEMCOS (GEneralized Message COntrol System), and an _____ subsidiary developed MCS called TPMCS (Transaction Processing MCS)
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: There were predecessor transaction processing environments which included GEMCOS (GEneralized Message COntrol System), and an Australian Burroughs subsidiary developed MCS called TPMCS (Transaction Processing MCS).

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: Thus you can efficiently service users (whether they require state or not) with _____
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: Thus you can efficiently service users (whether they require state or not) with MCSs. MCSs also provide the backbone of large-scale transaction processing.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: Around _____ an implementation of TCP/IP was developed principally for a U.S
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: Around 1988 an implementation of TCP/IP was developed principally for a U.S.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: DMALGOL is ALGOL extended for compiling the DMSII database software from database description files created by the DASDL (Data Access and _____) compiler
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: DMALGOL is ALGOL extended for compiling the DMSII database software from database description files created by the DASDL (Data Access and Structure Definition Language) compiler.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: Normal user-level programs obtain database access by using code written in application languages, mainly _____ and COBOL, extended with database instructions and transaction processing directives
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: DMALGOL is ALGOL extended for compiling the DMSII database software from database description files created by the DASDL (Data Access and Structure Definition Language) compiler. Database designers and administrators compile database descriptions to generate DMALGOL code tailored for the tables and indexes specified.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: The most notable feature of _____ is its preprocessing mechanisms to generate code for handling tables and indices
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: Database designers and administrators compile database descriptions to generate DMALGOL code tailored for the tables and indexes specified. Administrators never need to write DMALGOL themselves.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: DMALGOL is used to provide tailored access routines for _____ databases
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: DMALGOL is used to provide tailored access routines for DMSII databases.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: After a database is defined using the Data Access and _____ (DASDL), the schema is translated by the preprocessor into tailored DMALGOL access routines and then compiled
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: After a database is defined using the Data Access and Structure Definition Language (DASDL), the schema is translated by the preprocessor into tailored DMALGOL access routines and then compiled.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: This means that, unlike in other _____ implementations, there is often no need for database-specific if/then/else code at run-time
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: This means that, unlike in other DBMS implementations, there is often no need for database-specific if/then/else code at run-time.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: Roy Guck of Burroughs was one of the main developers of _____
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: Roy Guck of Burroughs was one of the main developers of DMSII.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: In later years, with compiler code size being less of a concern, most of the preprocessing constructs were made available in the user level of _____
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: An applications version of ALGOL to support the accessing of databases from application programs is called BDMSALGOL and included verbs like "FIND", "LOCK", "STORE", "GET", and "PUT" for database access and record manipulation. In later years, with compiler code size being less of a concern, most of the preprocessing constructs were made available in the user level of ALGOL.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: There are specific instruction to perform process switches: B5000, B5500, B5700 _____ P1 (IP1) and Initiate P2 (IP2) B6500, B7500 and successors MVST (move stack)
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: There are specific instruction to perform process switches: B5000, B5500, B5700 Initiate P1 (IP1) and Initiate P2 (IP2) B6500, B7500 and successors MVST (move stack).

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: User programs cannot issue an IP1, IP2 or _____, and there is only one place in the operating system where this is done
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: There are specific instruction to perform process switches: B5000, B5500, B5700 Initiate P1 (IP1) and Initiate P2 (IP2) B6500, B7500 and successors MVST (move stack). User programs cannot issue an IP1, IP2 or MVST, and there is only one place in the operating system where this is done.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: Another point for speed as promoted by the _____ designers was that processor speed is considerably faster if everything is on a single chip
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: Another point for speed as promoted by the RISC designers was that processor speed is considerably faster if everything is on a single chip.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: In fact, the A Series line of B5000 successors included the first single chip mainframe, the Micro-A of the late _____s
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: In fact, the A Series line of B5000 successors included the first single chip mainframe, the Micro-A of the late 1980s.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: This "mainframe" chip (named SCAMP for Single-Chip A-series _____) sat on an Intel-based plug-in PC board
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: This "mainframe" chip (named SCAMP for Single-Chip A-series Mainframe Processor) sat on an Intel-based plug-in PC board.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: Some few of _____'s successors therefore insist that — value parameters be read only – but most do not
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: Some few of ALGOL's successors therefore insist that — value parameters be read only – but most do not.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: This could cause difficulty for some systems that generated _____ source as output (tailored to solve some special problem) if the generation method frequently nested procedure within procedure
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: This could cause difficulty for some systems that generated Algol source as output (tailored to solve some special problem) if the generation method frequently nested procedure within procedure.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: The processed procedure still has access to the enclosing environment and this is a very efficient IPC (_____) mechanism
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: The processed procedure still has access to the enclosing environment and this is a very efficient IPC (Inter Process Communication) mechanism.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: This _____ mechanism is a basic enabler for multiprocessing in addition to multitasking
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: EVENTs also allow for mutual exclusion synchronization through the PROCURE and LIBERATE functions. This EVENT mechanism is a basic enabler for multiprocessing in addition to multitasking.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: Thus, _____ ALGOL had some of the multi-processing and synchronization features of later languages like Ada
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: Thus, Burroughs Extended ALGOL had some of the multi-processing and synchronization features of later languages like Ada.

Burroughs Large Systems.fact: And indeed, this was reflected in the form of the VALC instruction (value call) that loaded an operand onto the stack. The address part of the VALC operation thus reserved just three bits for that purpose, with the remainder being available for referring to entities at that and lower levels.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Burroughs Large Systems.fact: And indeed, this was reflected in the form of the VALC instruction (value call) that loaded an operand onto the stack. The address part of the VALC operation thus reserved just three bits for that purpose, with the remainder being available for referring to entities at that and lower levels.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Burroughs Large Systems.fact: The address part of the VALC operation thus reserved just three bits for that purpose, with the remainder being available for referring to entities at that and lower levels. Further, only the VALC opcode loaded data: opcodes for ADD, MULT and so forth did no addressing, working entirely on the top elements of the stack.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: In _____'s case, a multidimensional array would employ multiple levels of such addressing
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: In ALGOL's case, a multidimensional array would employ multiple levels of such addressing.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: The single-dimensional equivalent array, possibly segmented if large enough, would then be accessed in the same manner as a single-dimensional array in _____
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: The single-dimensional equivalent array, possibly segmented if large enough, would then be accessed in the same manner as a single-dimensional array in ALGOL.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: In _____'s case, this enabled the development of "ragged" arrays, rather than the usual fixed rectangular (or higher dimension) arrays
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: The single-dimensional equivalent array, possibly segmented if large enough, would then be accessed in the same manner as a single-dimensional array in ALGOL. In ALGOL's case, this enabled the development of "ragged" arrays, rather than the usual fixed rectangular (or higher dimension) arrays.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: The declaration of: _____ A [0:99] requested the allocation of 100 words of type REAL data space in memory
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: Not initialising an array to zero at the start therefore was encouraged by this, normally an unwise omission. Array equivalencing is also supported.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: EBCDIC _____ MY_EA [0:99] requested that the system allocated a 100 character array
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: The ARRAY declaration requested allocation of 48-bit data words which could be used to store any bit pattern but the general operational practice was that each allocated word was considered to be a REAL operand. The declaration of: ARRAY A [0:99] requested the allocation of 100 words of type REAL data space in memory.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: The immediately preceding discussion uses the _____ syntax implementation to describe ARRAY declarations, but the same functionality is supported in COBOL and FORTRAN
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: The immediately preceding discussion uses the ALGOL syntax implementation to describe ARRAY declarations, but the same functionality is supported in COBOL and FORTRAN. FORTRAN was not expected to support recursion and perhaps one stumbling block to people's understanding of how ALGOL was to be implemented was how to implement recursion.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: FORTRAN was not expected to support recursion and perhaps one stumbling block to people's understanding of how _____ was to be implemented was how to implement recursion
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: The immediately preceding discussion uses the ALGOL syntax implementation to describe ARRAY declarations, but the same functionality is supported in COBOL and FORTRAN. FORTRAN was not expected to support recursion and perhaps one stumbling block to people's understanding of how ALGOL was to be implemented was how to implement recursion.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: For instance, for subroutines and functions it checked that they were invoked with the correct number of parameters, as is normal for _____-style compilers
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: For instance, for subroutines and functions it checked that they were invoked with the correct number of parameters, as is normal for ALGOL-style compilers. In fact, Burroughs became known for its superior compilers and implementation of languages, including the object-oriented Simula (a superset of ALGOL), and Iverson, the designer of APL declared that the Burroughs implementation of APL was the best he'd seen.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: The current incarnation of these machines, the _____Path has extended tags further into a four bit tag
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: The current incarnation of these machines, the Unisys ClearPath has extended tags further into a four bit tag.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: The microcode level that specified four bit tags was referred to as level _____
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: The microcode level that specified four bit tags was called level Gamma.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: The _____ references data on any stack by including a stack number in the address
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: The SIRW references data on any stack by including a stack number in the address. Amongst other things, SIRW's are used to provide addressing between discrete process stacks such as those generated in response to the CALL and PROCESS statements.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: Amongst other things, _____'s are used to provide addressing between discrete process stacks such as those generated in response to the CALL and PROCESS statements
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: The SIRW references data on any stack by including a stack number in the address. Amongst other things, SIRW's are used to provide addressing between discrete process stacks such as those generated in response to the CALL and PROCESS statements.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: The _____ operator explicitly enters a procedure (non-value-returning routine)
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: Tag 7 is the program control word which describes a procedure entry point. The ENTR operator explicitly enters a procedure (non-value-returning routine).

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: Functions (value-returning routines) are implicitly entered by operators such as value call (_____)
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: Functions (value-returning routines) are implicitly entered by operators such as value call (VALC).

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: Tag 3 is also used for the stack control words _____, RCW, TOSCW
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: Tag 3 is also used for the stack control words MSCW, RCW, TOSCW.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: The architecture has two modes, _____ and Character Mode, and each has a separate repertoire of syllables
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: The architecture has two modes, Word Mode and Character Mode, and each has a separate repertoire of syllables.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: A processor may be either _____ or Normal State, and certain syllables are only permissible in Control State
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: A processor may be either Control State or Normal State, and certain syllables are only permissible in Control State.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: If we remove the operators reserved for the operating system such as _____ and HALT, the set of operators commonly used by user-level programs is less than 100
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: If we remove the operators reserved for the operating system such as MVST and HALT, the set of operators commonly used by user-level programs is less than 100.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: The Name Call and _____ syllables contain address couples; the Operator syllables either use no addresses or use control words and descriptors on the stack
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: The Name Call and Value Call syllables contain address couples; the Operator syllables either use no addresses or use control words and descriptors on the stack.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: RDLK (ReaD with _____) is a very low-level way of synchronizing between processors
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: RDLK (ReaD with LocK) is a very low-level way of synchronizing between processors.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: The higher level mechanism generally employed by user programs is the _____ data type
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: The higher level mechanism generally employed by user programs is the EVENT data type. The EVENT data type did have some system overhead.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: The _____ data type did have some system overhead
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: The higher level mechanism generally employed by user programs is the EVENT data type. The EVENT data type did have some system overhead.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: To avoid this overhead, a special locking technique called Dahm locks (named after a Burroughs software guru, _____) can be used
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: To avoid this overhead, a special locking technique called Dahm locks (named after a Burroughs software guru, Dave Dahm) can be used.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: Dahm locks used the READLOCK _____ language statement which generated a RDLK operator at the code level
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: Dahm locks used the READLOCK ALGOL language statement which generated a RDLK operator at the code level. The Algol compiler produced code to invoke this operator via a special function that enabled a "swap" operation on single-word data without an explicit temporary value.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: The B5000 stack architecture inspired _____, the designer of the programming language Forth, who encountered the B5500 while at MIT
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: The B5000 stack architecture inspired Chuck Moore, the designer of the programming language Forth, who encountered the B5500 while at MIT.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: In Forth - _____, Moore described the influence, noting that Forth's DUP, DROP and SWAP came from the corresponding B5500 instructions (DUPL, DLET, EXCH)
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: In Forth - The Early Years, Moore described the influence, noting that Forth's DUP, DROP and SWAP came from the corresponding B5500 instructions (DUPL, DLET, EXCH).

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: B5000 machines with their stack-based architecture and tagged memory also heavily influenced the _____ series of mainframes and supercomputers
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: B5000 machines with their stack-based architecture and tagged memory also heavily influenced the Soviet Elbrus series of mainframes and supercomputers.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: There existed a kind of an assembly language for them, called El-_____, but it was more or less a modification of ALGOL 68 and supported structured programming and first-class procedures
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: There existed a kind of an assembly language for them, called El-76, but it was more or less a modification of ALGOL 68 and supported structured programming and first-class procedures.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: Later generations of the series, though, switched away from this architecture to the _____-like VLIW CPUs
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: Later generations of the series, though, switched away from this architecture to the EPIC-like VLIW CPUs.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: Around _____, these systems migrated to MIPS RISC architecture but continued to support execution of stack machine binaries by object code translation or direct emulation
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: Around 1990, these systems migrated to MIPS RISC architecture but continued to support execution of stack machine binaries by object code translation or direct emulation.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: Sometime after _____, these systems migrated to Itanium architecture and continued to run the legacy stack machine binaries
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: Sometime after 2000, these systems migrated to Itanium architecture and continued to run the legacy stack machine binaries.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: Bob Barton was also very influential on _____
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: Bob Barton was also very influential on Alan Kay.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: Kay was also impressed by the data-driven tagged architecture of the B5000 and this influenced his thinking in his developments in object-oriented programming and _____
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: Kay was also impressed by the data-driven tagged architecture of the B5000 and this influenced his thinking in his developments in object-oriented programming and Smalltalk.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: One notable such product is the _____ JVM which provides a secure sandbox in which applications run
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: One notable such product is the Java JVM which provides a secure sandbox in which applications run.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: Among other customers of the B6700 and B7700 were all five _____ universities in 1971
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: Among other customers of the B6700 and B7700 were all five New Zealand universities in 1971.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: Starting in the early 1980's, the DCP technology was replaced by the ICP (_____) which provided LAN based connectivity for the mainframe system
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: Starting in the early 1980's, the DCP technology was replaced by the ICP (Integrated Communications Processor) which provided LAN based connectivity for the mainframe system.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: There existed a kind of an assembly language for them, called El-76, but it was more or less a modification of _____ 68 and supported structured programming and first-class procedures
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: There existed a kind of an assembly language for them, called El-76, but it was more or less a modification of ALGOL 68 and supported structured programming and first-class procedures.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: These machines were the _____ 100 through the Libra 500, with the Libra 590 being announced in 2005
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: These machines were the Libra 100 through the Libra 500, with the Libra 590 being announced in 2005. Later Libras, including the 590, also incorporate Intel Xeon processors and can run the Burroughs large systems architecture in emulation as well as on the MCP CMOS processors.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: The single-pass compiler for _____ could compile over 250 lines per second
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: Two levels of language extensions provide the additional constructs: ESPOL and NEWP for writing the MCP and closely related software, and DCALGOL and DMALGOL to provide more specific extensions for specific kinds of system software. ESPOL was used to write the Master Control Program (MCP) on Burroughs computer systems from the B5000 to the B6700.

Burroughs Large Systems.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs Large Systems.question: In fact, the A _____ line of B5000 successors included the first single chip mainframe, the Micro-A of the late 1980s
Burroughs Large Systems.fact: In fact, the A Series line of B5000 successors included the first single chip mainframe, the Micro-A of the late 1980s. This "mainframe" chip (named SCAMP for Single-Chip A-series Mainframe Processor) sat on an Intel-based plug-in PC board.

Burroughs MCP.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs MCP.question: The _____ was Mainframe computer operating system.
Burroughs MCP.fact: The MCP (Master Control Program) is the operating system of the Burroughs B5000/B5500/B5700 and the B6500 and successors, including the Unisys Clearpath/MCP systems. MCP was originally written in 1961 in ESPOL (Executive Systems Problem Oriented Language).

Burroughs MCP.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs MCP.question: The MCP (_____) is the operating system of the Burroughs B5000/B5500/B5700 and the B6500 and successors, including the Unisys Clearpath/MCP systems
Burroughs MCP.fact: The MCP (Master Control Program) is the operating system of the Burroughs B5000/B5500/B5700 and the B6500 and successors, including the Unisys Clearpath/MCP systems.

Burroughs MCP.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs MCP.question: MCP was originally written in _____ in ESPOL (Executive Systems Problem Oriented Language)
Burroughs MCP.fact: MCP was originally written in 1961 in ESPOL (Executive Systems Problem Oriented Language). The Burroughs Large System (B5000 and successors) were unique in that they were designed with the expectation that all software, including system software, would be written in an HLL rather than in assembly language, which was a unique and innovative approach in 1961.

Burroughs MCP.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs MCP.question: In the 1970s, MCP was converted to _____ which was a better structured, more robust, and more secure form of ESPOL
Burroughs MCP.fact: In the 1970s, MCP was converted to NEWP which was a better structured, more robust, and more secure form of ESPOL.

Burroughs MCP.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs MCP.question: Unlike IBM, which faced hardware competition after the departure of _____, Burroughs software only ever ran on Burroughs hardware due to a lack of compatible third party hardware
Burroughs MCP.fact: Unlike IBM, which faced hardware competition after the departure of Gene Amdahl, Burroughs software only ever ran on Burroughs hardware due to a lack of compatible third party hardware.

Burroughs MCP.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs MCP.question: At the time, this was common practice, and was necessary as it was not unusual for customers (especially large ones, such as the _____) to modify the program to fit their specific needs
Burroughs MCP.fact: At the time, this was common practice, and was necessary as it was not unusual for customers (especially large ones, such as the Federal Reserve) to modify the program to fit their specific needs.

Burroughs MCP.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs MCP.question: As a result, a _____ was formed, which held annual meetings and allowed users to exchange their own extensions to the OS and other parts of the system software suite
Burroughs MCP.fact: As a result, a Burroughs Users Group was formed, which held annual meetings and allowed users to exchange their own extensions to the OS and other parts of the system software suite.

Burroughs MCP.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs MCP.question: Burroughs was not the first manufacturer to distribute source code and was a late entry to electronic computing (compared to its traditional rivals NCR, IBM, and _____)
Burroughs MCP.fact: Burroughs was not the first manufacturer to distribute source code and was a late entry to electronic computing (compared to its traditional rivals NCR, IBM, and Univac).

Burroughs MCP.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Burroughs MCP.question: Now that MCP runs on commodity hardware, some elements of the MCP based software suite are no longer made available in source form by _____
